correctness.rationale: A vertex-geodesic of C_n contains at most floor(n/2)+1 vertices. All singleton/pair traces occur. If three are shattered, a shortest path through them has outer extremes at distance exactly n/2; otherwise their shorter unique subpath forces the omitted middle point, contradicting one required trace. Thus n is even and an antipodal pair is necessary; the two distinct semicircles plus subpaths and singleton outside explicitly realize all eight traces. Four vertices ordered on any geodesic force an omitted-middle contradiction for the pair (second,fourth), excluding size≥4. Count m(n-2)=n(n-2)/2 triangles. Odd Δ_n is K_n with cycle rank C(n-1,2). For even n=2m, each pair of antipodal edges spans a tetrahedron boundary whose four faces are precisely those triangles, remove one face from each; contract disjoint antipodal edges and retract complementing disks to arcs of K_m; reattach omitted 2-cells along nullhomotopic loops, giving wedge C(m-1,2) S¹ and C(m,2) S² integrally. Boundary n=3,4 and all-n proof checked. Independent exhaustive trace search and GF2 Betti at n=3..18 match, but do not establish integral homotopy.

value.rationale: This gives the entire simplicial complex of attainable traces and its integral homotopy type, not only the VC dimension. The parity-triggered S² summands quantify a genuinely topological jump from cycles with odd order to even order. Geodesic path range systems are natural combinatorial learning objects, and the exact homotopy classification is useful without a general-graph theorem.
